$comment: Lava (docs/proposals/VOLCANOES.md §6, phase V1): hot fluids on their own surface grid (`dwell-lava`), a depth and a heat per 1 m column, moving by the viscous gravity-current law (flow per metre of width = g × h³ × surface slope / (3 × viscosity), through the depth above `yieldDepthM`, so a thin front stands still), scheduled like the water: every lava tick near a player, fast-forwarded in one run elsewhere. Times are real seconds × `speed`. tickEvery: server ticks per lava tick near a player. nearRadiusM: a field with a player this close runs every lava tick. farEverySeconds: a far field runs the time it owes once it owes this much. cfl: a substep's share of the explicit law's stable step (cell² / (4 × the fastest face's g h³ / 3ν)). maxSubsteps: the most substeps one run takes (more, and the rest of its time is lost). stepDepthM (V2): a substep is sized for lava up to this deep; deeper ponds level through the flux limit (no face moves more than the stable share of its two surfaces' difference) instead of shrinking every substep. maxTiles (V2): a growing field's most tiles of 8 × 8 columns, the cap on its area (a field covers the tiles its lava reaches, and drops the ones all rock). fluids: each hot fluid, by name (`name`; a field and a vent name theirs): viscosityM2s (kinematic, m²/s; higher is slower), yieldDepthM (a depth that never flows: the front's crust), coolingSeconds (a column at rest, thinDepthM deep, from vent heat to rock), edgeCooling (how much faster per dry neighbour: lava cools from its edges), thinDepthM (lava this deep cools in coolingSeconds; thinner faster and deeper slower, in proportion: it cools from its top), tubeSpeedMs (V2: moving lava keeps its heat under its crust, a tube: its cooling is divided by 1 + speed / tubeSpeedMs, so a running river stays molten far from its vent and its front, once stopped, cools at the full rate), breakoutDepthM (V2: a pond this deep breaks out through the crust dam beside it on lower ground, its way down (a levee beside its channel, on ground as high, holds), the field's own rock melted again, so a river dammed by its frozen overflow runs on; 0 never), rock (the block it cools into: new land), quench (lava running into a water column: `rock` at once, raising the sea floor until it stands above the water as new land, the quench edge, and a steam event turning `steamWaterM` of the water's depth to steam), light (the light level its block gives, 0–15; the block itself comes with the look), damagePerSecond (health a second to a player in it), burnSeconds and burnDamagePerSecond (the burning after leaving it). Prototype tuning (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.1). Run `node shared/fluids/lava.mjs` after editing; CI fails if crates/dwell-lava/src/lava.gen.rs is stale.
$steam: The clients' steam puffs where lava boils water away (VOLCANOES.md §6.3): colour, life (s), rise (m/s), size at birth and end (m), peak opacity.
$burnEdge: The red-orange screen edge while the player burns (lava's Burn damage): colour, opacity at its strongest, seconds after a burn hit.
$heat: Lava's look by heat (owner, 2026-11-11: bright red-orange, darkening as it solidifies), hottest first: a column whose heat (0 vent hot, 0 rock) is at least `above` shows that stop. color (sRGB) the molten seams' glow, intensity its emissive (over 1 glows past the tone curve's white: the bloom picks it up), crust how much of the surface the dark crust plates cover (0 all molten, 1 all crust). heatHysteresis: a column moves to a hotter or cooler stop only once its heat is this far past the stop's edge, so a column at a threshold doesn't flicker between stops (the rate limit on writing them).
